exposure: Maternal risk factors (gestational diabetes, hypertension, anaemia, hypothyroidism)
cohort: The study included 100 late preterm neonates born between 34-36 6/7 weeks gestational age, excluding those with major anomalies, out-born babies, and stillbirths.
finding: Late preterm babies require longer hospital and NICU stays, increased medical interventions, and face higher risks of complications such as respiratory distress, jaundice, and suspect sepsis.
mod_finding: Among late preterm neonates, 68% were delivered by Caesarean section.
